title: SKU & Limit Migration Playbook for New Pricing Tiers
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Scope: Coordinate cross-functional launch of new SKUs, limits, and billing communications for the 2026 packaging update. Goals: ensure SKU mappings are complete, billing events are validated, tenant transitions are safe, sales and support have collateral and playbooks, and release notes + customer comms are approved. This ticket is the PM playbook and coordination hub for the end-to-end launch activities.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Final SKU table approved by Finance and Revenue Ops; 2) Billing events in prod validated on staging customers; 3) Automated migration scripts and rollback plan are tested; 4) Release notes drafted and signed off by Docs and Legal; 5) Sales enablement assets (pricing cheatsheet, objection handling, MRR examples) delivered; 6) Support runbook published in Confluence; 7) Launch announcement schedule set and sequencing agreed with Marketing.
tasks_checklist: Finalize SKU identifiers and human-friendly names (Finance/RevOps)
Define per-SKU rate limits and default quotas
Map old plan IDs to new SKUs and create migration matrix
Implement and test billing meter events for new SKU boundaries
Draft customer billing comms and migration FAQ
Create sales playbook and pricing calculator spreadsheet
Prepare console UX copy updates for plan selector
Run a dry-run migration on 3 pilot tenants
Sign off with Legal on TOS/price change language
Publish release notes and developer migration guide
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Metering mismatch causes overbilling. Mitigation: dual-run metering for two billing cycles, compare against baseline and alert on delta > 2%.
Risk: Confusion from SKU naming. Mitigation: keep internal IDs stable, publish human-friendly mapping and update console copy to show legacy equivalence.
Risk: Sales churn due to perceived price increase. Mitigation: build PRICING FAQ, targeted account outreach, and temporary grandfathering window for eligible customers.
Risk: Rollout race condition between console and billing. Mitigation: deploy billing changes first behind feature flag, open read-only window for console updates, then flip flags after verification.
release_notes_draft: Redwood Inference is introducing refreshed packaging to simplify product choices and better align pricing with usage patterns. Highlights: consolidated SKUs for inference, explicit embedding and retrieval quotas, and new limits for Dedicated capacity burst tiers. Customers will see mappings from legacy plans in the console and have a 30-day transition window. Billing will use the new SKU IDs starting on the effective date; we will run a staggered migration for existing customers and provide per-account migration details via email. See the developer migration guide for API compatibility notes and example billing events.
customer_comm_email_draft:
Subject: Upcoming changes to Redwood Inference plans and billing

Hi <Customer>,

On <effective_date> we will update our plan structure to provide clearer pricing and more predictable billing. This change consolidates several legacy plans into simplified SKUs and introduces explicit limits on embedding and burst capacity. You will receive a personalized migration summary in the next 7 days. No action is required for most customers — your usage will be migrated automatically and we will honor your current rates for eligible accounts for a limited period. If you expect significant impact, reply to this email and our Customer Success team will schedule a migration review.

Best,
Redwood Inference Billing Team

migration_matrix_snippet: LegacyPlanA -> SKU-Core-Standard | LegacyPlanB -> SKU-Core-Plus | LegacyPlanC -> SKU-Dedicated-Burst | Notes: LegacyPlanB customers with custom quotas will be migrated to SKU-Core-Plus with same token-based quotas preserved via account-level overrides.
validation_and_testing_plan: Unit tests for billing metering and SKU assignment
End-to-end billing integration test with sandboxed payment provider
Pilot migrations: 3 low-risk tenants, monitor invoicing for 2 billing cycles
Smoke tests: console displays, API responses, and webhook billing events
Chaos test: simulate partial failure during migration and validate rollback
